sources.name: AddressBase Fundamentals
sources.role: shared address-product design and quality-metadata contract
verified_facts: AddressBase Fundamentals covers identifiers, coordinate systems, classification, supply, currency, precision and source design shared by the family.
semantic_limits: Shared design guidance does not prove any specific row, source version, geometry or measurement.

sources.name: Unique Property Reference Number Fundamentals
verified_facts: A UPRN persists across address lifecycle changes and links related address records across datasets.
semantic_limits: Persistence does not make the UPRN a primary key for every table or an exact legal-boundary identifier.

sources.name: AddressBase Coordinate Reference Systems
sources.role: BNG and ETRS89 coordinate-role separation contract
verified_facts: AddressBase products contain British National Grid and ETRS89 coordinate representations with different reference-system semantics.
semantic_limits: Reprojection or dual coordinate fields do not improve positional accuracy or establish an orthometric height datum.

sources.name: AddressBase Classification Scheme
sources.role: hierarchical address classification and code-version contract
verified_facts: The scheme provides primary through more detailed classification levels whose availability varies by AddressBase product and record.
semantic_limits: A classification code describes use or type and must not be interpreted as geometry, ownership or elevation evidence.

sources.name: OS Open UPRN Documentation
sources.role: open identifier product, refresh and supply-format contract
verified_facts: OS Open UPRN is a six-weekly open identifier product supplied in CSV and GeoPackage for linking addressable locations.
semantic_limits: An open UPRN point is a representative location, not an HMLR title polygon or terrain-extrema sample.

sources.name: OS Open UPRN Overview
verified_facts: The product contains each AddressBase Premium record position with its UPRN, which remains stable when address details change.
semantic_limits: The address point must not be expanded into a cadastral extent or used as a substitute for exact polygon sampling.

sources.name: OS Open UPRN Technical Specification
sources.role: open UPRN feature-type and field contract
verified_facts: The technical specification defines the OS Open UPRN feature content while referring supply and CRS details to the overview.
semantic_limits: Technical conformance and a valid point do not prove the associated legal extent or height-difference metric.

sources.name: AddressBase Documentation
sources.role: matched postal/local-authority address and coordinate contract
verified_facts: AddressBase provides matched postal and local-authority address information with UPRNs and property-level coordinate attribution.
semantic_limits: A matched address record is not equivalent to the complete AddressBase Premium lifecycle record or an HMLR polygon.

sources.name: AddressBase Technical Specification
sources.role: BNG, ETRS89, classification and representative-point-quality contract
verified_facts: AddressBase records include British National Grid and ETRS89 coordinates, classification and a representative point code.
semantic_limits: Representative point quality describes an address location and must not be converted into parcel-boundary or elevation accuracy.

sources.name: AddressBase Supply and Update
verified_facts: The AddressBase supply specification distinguishes complete supplies from change-only updates and identifies product metadata.
semantic_limits: A change-only update cannot be used alone as a complete current address dataset without a compatible base supply.

sources.name: AddressBase Core Documentation
sources.role: current local-authority address, UPRN and property-coordinate contract
verified_facts: AddressBase Core provides more than 33 million addresses with UPRNs and property-level coordinates sourced from local-authority data.
semantic_limits: Record count and authoritative addressing do not establish exact title boundaries or terrain measurements.

sources.name: AddressBase Core Technical Specification
sources.role: core-address schema, identifier and supply contract
verified_facts: The technical specification defines AddressBase Core content and relies on AddressBase Fundamentals for shared identifier, CRS and classification rules.
semantic_limits: Core schema validity does not prove parcel identity, geometry containment or numeric height accuracy.

sources.name: AddressBase Plus Technical Specification
sources.role: current address, UPRN and TOID cross-reference contract
verified_facts: AddressBase Plus contains current postal and non-postal addresses with UPRNs and cross-references to OS MasterMap TOIDs.
semantic_limits: A TOID cross-reference links records but does not prove exact HMLR geometry, ownership or elevation.

sources.name: INSPIRE Index Polygons Spatial Data
sources.role: freehold registered-property location, monthly update and subset contract
verified_facts: INSPIRE Index Polygons contains locations of freehold registered property in England and Wales as a subset of the full Index Polygons and is updated monthly.
semantic_limits: INSPIRE geometry is an index-polygon dataset and must not be represented as a surveyed exact legal boundary.

sources.name: Title Plan — Practice Guide 40 Supplement 5
sources.role: title-plan purpose, general extent, scale and register-context contract
verified_facts: A title plan supports the register, shows the general extent and must be read with the register and referenced documents.
semantic_limits: The plan normally shows general boundaries; dimensions or red edging do not establish a surveyed exact boundary.

sources.name: Boundary Agreements and Determined Boundaries — Practice Guide 40 Supplement 4
sources.role: general versus determined boundary and filed-plan contract
verified_facts: A determined boundary records an exact line already identified through the required evidence and retained plan; HM Land Registry does not resolve the underlying dispute.
semantic_limits: A general title-plan boundary must not be promoted to a determined boundary without the formal determination record.
